To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Roma are not only the victims of racist violence but they are also the target of racist practices and policies in Europe, in the form of the everyday anti-Roma racism and the structural anti-Roma racism.
Roma are a stigmatized group in Europe, which is reflected in their daily experiences.
the Roma are a minority that has experienced centuries of discrimination, persecution, and exclusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how Roma in Europe experience the daily racism and structural racism and the trauma it produces in their lives.
the everyday racism against Roma and the traumatic effects of structural racism and its effects on the Roma population in Europe.
the ways in which Roma bodies are being disciplined in urban spaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Roma people in Europe are facing a situation where the state is using its power and authority in a way that makes them invisible, and therefore, not entitled to the rights that are granted by the state.
the Roma are not a homogeneous group and that they are not a single ethnic group.
the Roma are a people who are being discriminated against and excluded in Europe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how the Roma are being disciplined in Europe, and how they are disciplined in the name of security, integration, and human rights.
the paper examines the challenges of conceptualizing Roma experiences in an anti-Roma Europe, in the context of human rights, internal security and "integration" policies.
the Roma in Europe are facing a new form of racism, the "Anti Roma Europe" which is a new way to discipline and control the Roma bodies in urban spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Roma are not a homogenous group.
the Roma are a people who have been systematically de-humanised by a racist system.
the anti-Roma racism in Europe is a modern-day way of disciplining the body of Roma in urban spaces and the way of maintaining the Roma population as the Other.
